summary: Describes the MINIMAL addressing method and standard extensions for encoding fax numbers as email addresses, so mail systems can route a message to a fax machine. It was replaced by RFC 3192.

eli5.summary: A way to write a fax number so it looks like an email address, so a fax machine can receive your email.

questions: how to address a fax by email
how to write a fax number in email
subtitle: A standard format for putting fax numbers in email addresses.

tldr.problem: Email users and systems needed a standard way to send messages to fax machines, but there was no agreed format for encoding fax numbers as email addresses.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2304 defines a simple encoding format that starts with the service name FAX, then an equals sign, then the phone number in a standard international format, optionally followed by a subaddress. A domain name on the right identifies the gateway service.
tldr.outcome: This minimal format let email systems reliably route messages to fax machines without changing existing email software. It was later superseded by RFC 3192, which defined a broader solution.

facts.label: Phone number format
facts.value: + followed by digits, hyphens, or dots

today: RFC 3192 superseded RFC 2304 with a more comprehensive solution for telephone number mapping in email. RFC 2304 remains historically important as the original minimal specification.

sections.title: Why Fax over Email
sections.content:
Email users wanted to send faxes from their email interface, and organizations wanted to save money by routing fax traffic through cheaper email networks instead of the traditional phone system. To make this work, someone had to invent a standard way to write a fax number that looks like an email address, so routers and gateways would recognize it and deliver it to the right fax machine.

RFC 2304 describes the minimal set of rules needed for this to work. It does not try to solve the entire problem of PSTN (traditional telephone) addressing, just the core case that email systems could handle reliably.
sections.eli5: This RFC answers: how do I write a fax number so an email program can read it and send it to a fax machine?

sections.title: The Format of a Fax Email Address
sections.content:
A fax email address has three parts. The local part (left of the @) contains the fax information: it starts with the word FAX, then an equals sign, then a phone number in the format + followed by digits and optional separators like hyphens or dots. Optionally it can include /T33S= followed by a subaddress, which is a number that identifies a department or device on the same fax line.

The domain part (right of the @) is a normal Internet domain name that identifies the fax gateway service. Examples are FAX=+3940226338@faxworld.org or FAX=+12027653000/T33S=1387@faxworld.org.

The RFC allows optional slashes before and after the fax information (like /FAX=+33-1-88335215/@faxworld.org) to work with other gateway systems, but senders should omit them if possible.
sections.eli5: Write it like: FAX=+phonenumber@domain.com. The plus sign means international format. You can add /T33S=number at the end to reach a specific device on the same fax line, like an extension.

sections.title: Phone Number Rules
sections.content:
The RFC defines two ways to write phone numbers in a fax address. The standard way is global format: start with a plus sign, then the country code and the number, with optional hyphens or dots for readability (like +33-1-88335215). The plus sign tells systems this is a standard international number.

Alternative dialling schemas (like private company extensions or local numbering) are allowed, but they MUST NOT use a plus sign, and other systems can ignore them. The RFC does not define these alternatives; it only reserves the plus sign for the standard global format.

Implementers should accept hyphens and dots but remove them before processing, because they are only for humans to read.
sections.eli5: Phone numbers in fax email look like international phone numbers: +1-202-765-3000. The plus sign means it is a real country code. Hyphens and dots are OK for readability but the system ignores them.

sections.title: How Gateways Deliver Fax Messages
sections.content:
A fax email gateway is an Internet domain that accepts fax email addresses and converts them to real fax transmissions. It sits between the email system and the fax network. When an email arrives addressed to FAX=+3940226338@faxworld.org, the gateway extracts the phone number, verifies the format, and sends the message content as a fax to that number.

Multiple subaddresses for the same fax number are handled by sending separate messages to the MTA (mail transfer agent) for each subaddress. The user agent (email client) may accept multiple T33S values from the user, but must generate separate fax-email elements when passing the message to the mail system.
sections.eli5: The gateway service sits at the @domain.com part. It reads the fax number from your email and converts it to a real fax transmission on the phone network.
